tickets.note: No booking fee, no service charge.

intro.heading: The festival of lights returns to the Atomium
body: For ten years the Brussels Diwali Festival has filled the esplanade of the Atomium with music, dance, food and light. It is the largest celebration of Diwali in Belgium.

The tenth edition carries the theme Culture United. For the first time, European embassies and cultural institutes join us, each pairing a tradition of their own with an Indian one, along an avenue of lights running the length of the esplanade.

pillars.title: The lamps are lit for a reason
body: Diwali is the festival of lights, and the lights are lit for a reason. This is the part of the festival that says why.
Every year we build a small temple on the esplanade, a tent decorated by hand, and a purohit conducts a peace and harmony puja on both days.
Everyone is welcome, whatever they believe. You do not need to be Hindu, or to know what to do. You can stand and watch, and most people do.

pillars.title: The kitchens and the bazaar
body: Regional cooking from across India, made by people who cook it at home: Punjabi, Gujarati, South Indian, Bengali, street food from Mumbai and Delhi. Alongside it a bazaar of crafts, textiles and sweets, and bars along the length of the esplanade.
For a great many of our visitors this is where they taste Indian food properly for the first time, cooked the way it is cooked in India rather than the way it is cooked for Europe.
Everything on site is card only. There is no cash on the esplanade.

pillars.title: One stage, both days
body: Classical and contemporary Indian music, and dance from across the subcontinent: Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Bhangra, Garba. Performers from Belgium and from India, many of whom first trained at our own conservatory in Brussels.
In 2026 the stage carries the theme Culture United. European embassies and cultural institutes join us, each pairing a tradition of their own with an Indian one.

pillars.title: Fireworks over the Atomium
body: As the light goes, the esplanade fills. Bhangra and Bollywood, dhol, five thousand people dancing under the spheres, and fireworks each evening.

It is the largest celebration of Diwali in Belgium and the biggest Bollywood party in Europe. It does not feel like a polite cultural evening. It feels like a party that happens to be five hundred years old.

practical.a: Heysel / Heizel on metro line 6, two minutes from the esplanade. Tram 7 and 51 stop nearby. Parking C is a short walk. We would rather you came by metro, the site fills quickly and parking does not.
Every bar and kitchen on site takes card and contactless only. There is no cash on the esplanade and no cash machine. Bring a card or your phone.

Children under 12 come free, but they still need an event band. Register them with the rest of your booking and give their date of birth, so we know how many people are on site. Everyone is given an event band at the gate, adults included. The date of birth is used only to check age and to count numbers on site, and it is deleted after the festival. There is a children's area with workshops and storytelling.
The festival goes ahead in any weather, the stage is covered and much of the food is under canvas. Tickets are not refundable for rain. Bring a coat; Brussels in October is Brussels in October.

The esplanade is flat and step-free throughout. Accessible toilets are next to the stage. If you are coming with a wheelchair or need assistance, write to us beforehand and we will make sure someone meets you at the gate.

panels.a: For the tenth edition we have invited European embassies and cultural institutes to celebrate alongside us. Each brings a tradition of their own and pairs it with an Indian one: a duet, a shared dish, a dance answered by another dance. Diwali is a festival of light, and light is not the property of one country.
A path of lamps runs the length of the esplanade, from the Heysel metro to the foot of the Atomium, each stretch given to a participating country. It is lit from dusk on both evenings.

The first Brussels Diwali was held in 2016. Since 2017 it has taken place on the esplanade of the Atomium, growing from a community gathering into the largest celebration of Diwali in Belgium, and one that is now as Belgian as it is Indian.
